# Repository metadata and settings

Repository: https://github.com/aalampatil/file-convert

## Description

Self-hosted Next.js file converter for Markdown, Word, PDF, and images, with private uploads, live progress, and automatic file expiry.

Suggested topics: `nextjs`, `typescript`, `file-converter`, `markdown-to-pdf`, `docx-to-pdf`, `pdf-to-docx`, `self-hosted`.

The same description is stored in package.json. Git-tracked files do not change GitHub's About description or repository settings by themselves.

Verified through GitHub's API on 2026-11-12: the About description and topics are applied, Issues are enabled, and private vulnerability reporting and vulnerability alerts are enabled. Recheck these settings when transferring or forking the repository.

## Maintainer settings

- Enable Issues so issue forms work.
- Enable private vulnerability reporting under Settings → Code security when available.
- Enable dependency graph, Dependabot alerts, and security updates.
- Protect `main` with a ruleset requiring pull requests, review, and the `quality` and `browser` checks from CI. Apply rules in a way that allows the owner to maintain this repository.
- Review Actions permissions; workflows need read-only repository contents.
- Keep secrets outside the repository and use least-privilege workflow tokens.
- Require discussions and reports to follow CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and SECURITY.md.
- Review the GitHub Community Profile after these files reach the default branch.

README, LICENSE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, SUPPORT, issue forms, and a pull request template are included. GitHub's community checks only see them after commits are pushed. Remote settings and enabled reporting features must be verified separately; the presence of these files is not evidence that those settings are enabled.
